summary: Pidilite makes glues, sealants, waterproofing coatings and tile adhesives sold under brands such as Fevicol, Fevikwik, M-Seal, Dr. Fixit and Roff. It also makes industrial adhesives, resins and pigments for other factories.
description: Pidilite makes products that stick, seal, waterproof and colour. The best known are glues used by carpenters, plumbers, painters and households. It also makes sealants that fill gaps and stop leaks, coatings that keep water out of roofs and walls, adhesives for fixing tiles, and art and craft colours. A smaller part of the business sells industrial adhesives, resins and pigments (fine coloured powders) to factories that make packaging, furniture, textiles, paints, printing inks, paper and leather. It sells across India and in 74 countries.
money: Pidilite earns money by selling branded products in tubes, bottles and tins through wholesalers, distributors, retailers and online platforms, and by selling industrial products to factories. Its main costs are the chemicals it buys, factory costs, advertising, and training and loyalty programmes for tradespeople. The report says input costs were benign in 2025-26, which let it spend more on its brands. A customer's payment is revenue, not profit.
customers: In the branded business, households, students, offices and tradespeople such as carpenters, painters, plumbers and mechanics use the products, but the wholesaler or shop buys from Pidilite and the user pays at the counter. In the business-to-business part, factories that make packaging, joinery, textiles, paints, printing inks, paper and leather buy industrial adhesives, resins and pigments directly.
drivers: How many units it sells (the report calls this underlying volume growth), the cost of its chemical raw materials compared with its prices, and how much it spends to keep its brands known and in tradespeople's hands.

groups.title: Glues for wood and the home
groups.examples: Fevicol white glue for furniture and Fevikwik instant glue for quick repairs.
groups.explanation: Pidilite's website says Fevicol, launched in 1959, is a white synthetic resin glue first made for carpenters, who then used glue made from animal fat. It says Fevikwik fixes in five seconds and is sold in hardware stores, grocers and stationery shops.

groups.title: Sealants and repair
groups.examples: M-Seal putty to mend a leaking pipe, and sealant to fill gaps in a bathroom.
groups.explanation: The website describes M-Seal as products to repair leaks, join pipes and fill gaps and cracks. In plain terms, an epoxy putty is a clay-like material that hardens after mixing.

groups.title: Waterproofing
groups.examples: Dr. Fixit coatings for a roof slab or an outside wall.
groups.explanation: The website says leakage and dampness damage new and old buildings and that Dr. Fixit offers coatings and other construction chemicals to stop it.

groups.title: Tile and stone fixing
groups.examples: Roff adhesive for fixing floor tiles, and grout to fill the joints.
groups.explanation: The website says Roff supplies adhesives and other products for fixing tiles and stone, as an alternative to cement.

groups.title: Art and craft
groups.examples: Fevicryl paints for glass and fabric, and fabric glue for beads and lace.
groups.explanation: The website says Fevicryl serves hobbyists with colours and accessories. The report counts art and craft materials within the branded Consumer and Bazaar segment.

groups.title: Industrial adhesives, resins and pigments
groups.examples: Adhesive used in packaging and footwear, resins, and pigments (coloured powders) sold to factories.
groups.explanation: The report's business-to-business segment sells these to factories in packaging, joinery, textiles, paints, printing inks, paper and leather. It lists footwear and the automotive industry among users of industrial adhesives.

basics.title: What are the report's two segments?
basics.text: Consumer and Bazaar means branded products bought by households and tradespeople through shops and markets (bazaars). Business to Business means products sold directly to factories. The report gives sales shares for each.

basics.title: What is underlying volume growth?
basics.text: The report uses the shorthand UVG (underlying volume growth). In plain terms, this means growth in the quantity sold, not growth that comes only from price rises.

basics.title: What are standalone and consolidated results?
basics.text: Standalone means Pidilite alone. Consolidated means Pidilite together with its subsidiaries in India and abroad. The report's segment shares are for the company alone, so check which one a number uses.

steps.title: Buy chemicals and packaging
steps.text: Pidilite buys raw materials for its products. The report says it keeps alternate suppliers and stock buffers for critical inputs.

steps.title: Make and pack
steps.text: Plants mix the chemicals and fill tubes, bottles, tins and drums.

steps.title: Sell through shops or direct to factories
steps.text: Branded products go to wholesalers, distributors, retailers and online platforms. Industrial products are sold to factories.

steps.title: Win over the tradesperson
steps.text: Carpenters, plumbers and tile fitters often choose the product for the job, so Pidilite runs clubs and training for them. It is a cost that comes before the sale.

steps.title: Bill and collect
steps.text: Revenue (what Pidilite bills), profit (what is left after costs) and cash received are different things, and timing of payment from wholesalers affects cash.

specifics.title: Tradespeople influence the choice
specifics.text: The website says that when Fevicol first came in a tube in 1970 it bypassed stores and approached carpenters directly. Pidilite now runs contractor clubs such as the Fevicol Champions Club and a similar club for waterproofing contractors.

specifics.title: Most sales are branded products
specifics.text: The report says the branded Consumer and Bazaar segment was 81.6 percent of the company's sales in 2025-26, business-to-business 18.0 percent and other items 0.4 percent (page 60 of the annual report, a downloadable document), so shop-counter demand matters more than factory orders.

specifics.title: Subsidiaries sit outside the company's own sales
specifics.text: The report's sales shares are for Pidilite alone. Its subsidiaries in India and its overseas subsidiaries in Dubai, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Thailand and Kenya are reported separately.

specifics.title: Mostly sold at home
specifics.text: Exports were 7.01 percent of the company's turnover, so Indian homes and building work drive most results.

watch: Can volume growth stay strong without price rises?
The company points to growth in units sold, which is a healthier sign than growth from price rises alone.
Compare underlying volume growth with sales growth and the average price change in each quarterly results release over several years.
How far do chemical prices rise after the West Asia conflict, and can prices follow?
The report says prices of all major inputs rose steeply and warns that further rises could reduce demand.
Compare gross margin and the input cost comments in each results release over the next year, and read the outlook section of the annual report.
The report says the business-to-business subsidiaries reported lower sales and profit, and exports were hit by tariffs.
Compare segment results for Business to Business with Consumer and Bazaar over several years.
How do the two segments compare in profit?
The company gives separate results for each segment. A segment that sells more is not always the one that earns more.
Read the segment note in the annual report and the segment table in each results release, and compare profit as a share of sales for each segment.
Are fake products a growing problem?
The report lists counterfeits as a risk to brand trust and user safety.
Look for any comments on enforcement actions or lost sales from counterfeits in the annual report.
risks: Dependence on single suppliers for key materials
The report names single-source or dominant suppliers as a risk. If one shuts down, production of the products that use that material can stop.

The report says that, because of the conflict in West Asia, prices of all major inputs rose steeply and shipping through a key sea route was disrupted. It warns this could raise prices and affect demand.
The report says counterfeits can harm goodwill, consumer trust and the safety of users of its products.
The report lists non-compliance with plastic waste laws as a risk and says it meets its producer responsibility requirements for packaging.
context: January to March 2026: sales and volumes up on a year earlier

The company's press release of 7 May 2026 says net sales for the quarter to 31 March 2026 grew 15.3 percent from the same quarter a year earlier, with underlying volume growth also 15.3 percent. These are standalone figures, meaning Pidilite alone without its subsidiaries.
sources: Pidilite press release, 7 May 2026 (quarter and year to 31 March 2026)
Pidilite website, Dr. Fixit brand page

financialNotes.title: Figures awaiting verification
financialNotes.text: Pidilite's revenue, profit and segment figures are pending verification against the filed results, so none are shown here. The report gives both standalone figures (Pidilite alone) and consolidated figures (with subsidiaries), so scope must be stated with every number.

stepsTitle: From a chemical plant to a shop counter.

quick.title: What it does
quick.text: It makes glues, sealants, waterproofing, tile adhesives and art colours for homes and tradespeople, and industrial adhesives, resins and pigments for factories.

quick.title: Who pays
quick.text: Wholesalers, distributors and shops buy the branded products, and factories buy the industrial ones directly. Households and tradespeople are the final users.

quick.title: How it earns
quick.text: It sells branded products in small packs in large volumes, and industrial products to factories.

quick.title: What it spends on
quick.text: Chemical raw materials, factories, advertising and brand building, and programmes that train and reward tradespeople.

helps.title: Brands that tradespeople and homes ask for
helps.text: The company says its Fevicol brand has become synonymous with adhesives to millions in India and is ranked among the most trusted brands in the country. This is the company's own statement.

helps.title: No term loans
helps.text: The report says Pidilite has no outstanding term loans, so interest on borrowing is not a large cost and it can keep spending on brands and new products.

helps.title: Demand follows building and repair work
helps.text: The report says home improvement offers room for growth because of new construction and renovation, and that government spending on infrastructure supports demand for its products.

hurts.title: Weather can delay project work
hurts.text: The report says one business-to-business subsidiary had delays in carrying out its project work because of extended monsoons and winter environmental restrictions, which lowered its sales and profit.

hurts.title: Tariffs and conflicts reduce exports
hurts.text: The report says the imposition of tariffs in key markets affected exports to those markets, and the quarterly release says industrial export revenue was affected by the conflict in the Middle East.

hurts.title: Many rivals large and small
hurts.text: The report says that in both segments there are a few medium to large companies with national reach and a large number of small regional companies, and multinationals are present in many product lines.
